purpose: How a licensed, certified Medicare-focused agent runs the years after the application: reading renewal compensation, per-member rate-year status, agent-of-record position and recoupment as regulated mechanisms whose current-year terms are verified rather than remembered; operating a year-round service desk for provider, drug-cost, denial, billing and status-change events inside the educational limits of the agent's role; running an annual review that leaves 'no change' as a respectable outcome; and keeping the book stable through service quality, vulnerable-consumer care and compliant referral growth rather than pressure.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

compensation amounts, payment levels, cycles and recoupment periods are treated as regulated mechanisms whose current-year values must be read from the applicable published schedule and each carrier's own compensation addendum, never recalled from a prior year or from a recruiter's illustration

every rule referenced here is named as an obligation class only; federal, state, carrier and upline requirements change by plan year and must be verified in the agent's own jurisdiction and signed contracts before any action is taken
the content is educational and operational for the agent's own practice, and is not personalized insurance, medical, legal or tax advice to any beneficiary

the members in this book are largely older adults and disabled beneficiaries, a protected population, so contact discipline and comprehension checks are treated as operating requirements rather than courtesies
the agent holds the credentials, certifications and carrier appointments required to service and be compensated on the book; loss of any of them changes what may be done for a member
exclusions: the credentialing stack itself — state license and continuing education, annual certification, carrier contracting, errors-and-omissions coverage, upline hierarchy and release mechanics — which is the Certifications, Contracts & Compliant Marketing KB's territory and is referenced here, never re-derived

the catalog of CMS marketing and communication rules, permission-to-contact and scope-of-appointment artifact rules, lead-vendor and event rules, and the audit-ready file standard — all owned by the Certifications, Contracts & Compliant Marketing KB; this KB only detects when one of those rules has been triggered and stops

enrollment-period determination, eligibility-window classification and the need-driven plan comparison and enrollment conversation itself — owned by the Enrollment Periods, Plan Comparison & Needs Fit KB; a servicing event that may justify an election is routed there rather than resolved here
recommending a specific plan to a specific beneficiary, or making an election on the beneficiary's behalf; every election belongs to the beneficiary

any specific commission dollar amount, percentage rate, published schedule figure, renewal multiple or book valuation stated as fact; all such quantities appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands to be verified per carrier and plan year
acting as a beneficiary's appointed representative in an appeal or grievance, arguing medical necessity, completing clinical forms, or giving medical, legal or tax advice
non-health lines of business such as life, annuity and property-casualty products, and employer group benefits administration
carrier internal operations: claims adjudication, provider contracting, formulary construction and plan pricing

competency_questions.question: What actually keeps a payment coming on a member I already enrolled, and how do I verify that for this plan year instead of trusting last year's understanding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer describes compensation as a mechanism (product class, schedule ceiling, carrier contract rate, payment path, payment cycle), names the per-member determination that sets initial versus renewal level and continuation, and states where the current-year values are verified

competency_questions.question: A plan change is clearly better for this member but it costs me compensation or triggers a recoupment — how do I decide, and what has to be in the file afterward?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer states that the member-side facts decide, that the compensation consequence is never a reason on either side, and that the file carries the provider, drug, cost or service reason recorded at the time of the decision

competency_questions.question: How do I know whether I am still the agent of record on a member, and what do I do when I find out I am not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer explains that agent-of-record is a carrier-side attribute set and moved by enrollment events rather than by the servicing relationship, names how status is verified per carrier, and gives a course of action that neither pressures the member nor abandons them

competency_questions.question: A carrier statement does not match the members I believe I have — how do I find the gap, dispute it with evidence, and how should the timing of this income shape my planning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer describes member-level reconciliation against the agent's own ledger, the cause classes for a missing or wrong line, the evidence a dispute needs and its filing window, and describes income timing as a seasonal mechanism in relative bands rather than as figures

competency_questions.question: A client calls in the middle of the year because a specialist has left the network — what is the correct sequence of steps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer confirms the fact at the source before advising, describes the member's exposure under their plan type in educational terms, and routes any election question to the enrollment path with permissions re-established rather than asserting that a right to change exists

competency_questions.question: A client's drug cost jumped at the pharmacy counter — how do I work out which mechanism produced it and what legitimate help exists?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer separates the candidate causes (formulary or tier change, coverage-phase movement, utilization-management requirement, pharmacy status, subsidy or Medicaid status change, new prescription) and routes to pharmacy, prescriber, carrier exception process or official assistance channels without the agent choosing drugs or promising coverage

competency_questions.question: A claim was denied or an unexpected bill arrived — how far can I help before I am acting outside my role?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer requires the actual notice before advising, classifies the stated denial reason, protects the deadline printed on it, routes to provider billing, carrier or the plan's appeal and grievance process, and states plainly what the agent must not do

competency_questions.question: At what exact point does a service call become a marketing or sales contact, and what has to exist before it goes any further?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer names the observable triggers that cross the line, requires the conversation to stop until the required permission and appointment artifacts are in place, and records who raised the topic first

competency_questions.question: How do I run an annual review that is genuinely need-driven, fits inside the contact rules, and treats 'nothing needs to change' as a complete outcome?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer prepares from the member file before contact, reviews the member's own plan changes first, requires the appointment artifact before any specific alternative is discussed, and documents a stay decision with the same rigor as a change

competency_questions.question: Which clients should I contact proactively and how often, and how does that change when a member is impaired or a family member starts speaking for them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer segments the book by service need rather than by expected payment, sets a cadence that stays inside consent and contact rules, and requires documented authority before anyone other than the beneficiary directs a decision

competency_questions.question: What life events in a member's circumstances do I need to notice, and what do I do with one when I find it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer lists the detectable status-change classes and their detection sources, records the change in the member file, tells the member what class of question it raises, and hands the window and eligibility determination to the enrollment path

competency_questions.question: My book lost more members than usual this year — how do I read that, and which of my own practices does it tell me to change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer separates structural exits from fit failures, service failures and agent-of-record losses, cohorts the leavers, and names the upstream practice each failure class sends work back to

competency_questions.question: How do I grow from a satisfied book by referral without breaking contact rules or inducement rules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer requires the referred person's own permission before contact, forbids anything of value that would be a prohibited inducement and any use of one member's protected information to reach another, and keeps referral requests out of vulnerable-member service calls

competency_questions.question: What do I actually hold when I call this book mine, and what happens to these members if I move upline, lose an appointment or stop practicing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer describes the book as a set of appointments and agent-of-record positions governed by carrier and upline contract terms that must be read as signed, refuses to promise permanence to members, and states a continuity plan that leaves members served

glossary.definition: The payment class that continues on a member who stays enrolled beyond the initial payment period, as distinct from the payment for a first-time enrollment. Its existence, level and duration are set by the applicable regulated schedule class and the carrier's contract; treat the amount and the cycle as values to verify per carrier and plan year, never as remembered constants.

The per-member determination of which payment level applies, derived from that member's enrollment history — whether they are new to the product class, continuously enrolled, or moving between plans in a way the rules treat as preserving or resetting the level. It is determined member by member against current-year guidance, not assumed from the agent's own tenure.

The carrier-side attribute recording which appointed agent is credited with, and paid on, a given member. It is set by the accepted enrollment and can move when the member enrolls through another agent, a carrier's own line or a public channel; providing service does not by itself create or restore it.

An enrolled member with no active agent of record — typically because the writing agent left, lost the appointment or was terminated. Orphans may be assigned or may simply call whoever answers; servicing one is legitimate work that may carry no compensation, and the decision of how to serve them is made deliberately rather than by accident.

The reversal of compensation already paid, triggered by mechanisms such as an early disenrollment within the period the rules define, a retroactive termination for non-payment or ineligibility, a reversed enrollment, or a reclassification of the payment level. Both the triggering period and the recovery method are contract and rule classes to be verified per carrier.

The yearly notice a plan sends its members describing what changes for the coming plan year — cost sharing, formulary, network and benefit changes. It is the trigger document for the annual review cycle and the first thing an agent reads for a member before comparing anything else.

The pattern of members staying enrolled and attributed over time. Read as a diagnostic rather than a target: high persistency usually indicates fit quality and responsive service, while a drop points at a specific upstream cause class such as fit failure, service failure or agent-of-record loss.

A contact whose purpose is helping a member use the coverage they already have — a card, a bill, a pharmacy rejection, a provider question. It becomes a marketing or sales contact the moment a different plan or a new election enters the conversation, at which point the permission and appointment requirements of the marketing-rule layer apply.

The set of members on whom the agent holds an agent-of-record position across carriers, together with the servicing relationships around them. It is held under carrier and upline contract terms rather than owned outright; portability, release and succession are determined by those signed agreements.

The free, unbiased counseling channel available to beneficiaries in each state. It is a legitimate referral destination when a member needs help the agent may not give — representation in an appeal, comparison assistance with no agent involved, or a second opinion the beneficiary wants from a non-selling source.

nodes.definition: Fix what the relationship becomes once the application is accepted: a standing service relationship that lasts as long as the member holds the plan and the agent holds the appointment, with an explicitly bounded promise on both sides. The agent owes reachability, plain-language explanation of coverage the member already has, help using the plan, escalation of what only a carrier or a government channel can resolve, and a current record; the beneficiary keeps every election decision. Equally, the frame states what the agent does not do — adjudicate claims, give medical, legal or tax advice, represent the member in an appeal, or promise an outcome a carrier controls. This unit comes first because most compliance and reputation failures in a mature book happen after enrollment, in casual calls where nobody thought a rule was in play.

included: the standing post-enrollment service promise and its stated limits
the division of labor between agent, carrier and government channels
the rule that elections remain the beneficiary's
excluded: the pre-enrollment marketing and appointment rules
enrollment-window determination
claims adjudication and clinical judgment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, carrier audit finding or repeated member confusion shows the stated service promise and its limits are not what members actually experience

pros.claim: A stated promise with stated limits converts a vague loyalty into a service others can hold you to, which is what keeps a member calling you rather than a carrier sales line
pros.example: a member with a denied claim calls the agent first and gets a documented escalation with a named next step, instead of calling a sales number and being enrolled elsewhere by whoever answered

cons.claim: An open-ended service promise creates workload the compensation mechanism never sized, and the overload lands exactly when the annual window is open
cons.example: one member with a specialty drug, three specialists and a billing dispute can absorb the servicing capacity of dozens of stable members during the weeks the review queue is longest

failure_modes: treating the accepted application as the end of the relationship and reappearing only when a change would pay
drifting into clinical or claims judgment because the member asked and nobody else answered
promising outcomes controlled by the carrier so that the agent absorbs blame for a decision they never made
acceptance_tests: the service promise given to members states what the agent will do, what only the carrier or a government channel can do, and how to reach the agent
a sampled servicing call shows the agent explaining coverage the member already holds without recommending an alternative plan
revisit_triggers: a carrier appointment or certification lapses so that servicing a segment of the book is no longer permitted
recurring member complaints show the promise is understood differently by members than by the agent

nodes.definition: The standing rule that no difference in how an outcome pays the agent may enter a servicing recommendation, an annual-review agenda, or a retention effort. In an established book the temptation is structural rather than dramatic: moving a member between plans can reset their payment level, keeping them can preserve it, an early move can reverse money already paid, and the agent knows all of this while the member does not. The rule is that the member's own providers, drugs, costs and stability decide; that the agent's economics are never a stated or unstated reason; and that whenever a compensation consequence exists in either direction, the member-side reason for the outcome is recorded at the time it is made, so the decision is defensible years later. Which consequences apply is itself verified against current-year schedule classes rather than assumed.

included: the neutrality rule for every stay-or-move decision in the book
recording the member-side reason at the moment of decision
symmetry of documentation between stay decisions and change decisions
excluded: the enrollment-time comparison method itself
the marketing-rule catalog
any statement of what a given decision pays

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published change to compensation schedule classes, or an enforcement action or carrier bulletin describing what steering looks like in practice

pros.claim: It disarms the single most damaging allegation class in this vertical — that the agent moved members for money
pros.example: a file note reading 'stayed on current plan: both specialists in network for next year and all five drugs remain on the formulary tier the member can afford' answers a churning allegation without the agent having to reconstruct intent

cons.claim: Genuine neutrality regularly costs the agent the only compensation event a household would have produced that year
cons.example: telling a member whose plan still fits that there is nothing to do ends the conversation with no new enrollment, in the same weeks a competitor is writing changes

failure_modes: constructing a member-side rationale after the fact for a move whose real driver was the payment level
staying silent about an option that fits better because it pays less or triggers a reversal
building the annual-review call list from expected payment rather than from member need
acceptance_tests: every plan change in the book carries a member-side reason recorded before the change, and no file cites the agent's compensation as a factor
a sample of stay decisions is documented to the same standard as a sample of change decisions
the annual-review queue can be shown to be ordered by member need and review timing, not by expected payment
revisit_triggers: schedule classes or carrier compensation addenda change for the coming plan year
a carrier audit, secret shop or complaint questions a pattern of movement in the book
an unusual concentration of changes appears in one plan, one cohort or one month

nodes.definition: Operate every contact on the assumption that the person on the other end may be older, hard of hearing, cognitively variable, isolated, or already being worked by someone less scrupulous. Concretely: contact only through channels the member agreed to and at humane hours; speak in plain language and check comprehension by asking the member to say back what will happen next rather than asking whether they understood; never use urgency, loss framing or invented deadlines to force a decision; slow down or stop when confusion appears and offer to continue when a person the member chooses can be present; accept a family member's involvement only with the member's own authorization on file, and never let a caregiver's preference override a competent beneficiary; and recognize and escalate suspected exploitation through official channels. Honor a do-not-contact request immediately and permanently.

included: pace, language and comprehension checks in every contact
authorization requirements before a third party directs anything
recognition and escalation of pressure or exploitation
immediate honoring of contact preferences
excluded: the permission-to-contact and appointment artifact rules themselves
capacity determinations, which are not the agent's to make
any clinical assessment of the member

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: updated regulator or carrier guidance on contact with protected consumers, or a pattern of complaints alleging pressure or confusion in the book

pros.claim: Comprehension checks catch the misunderstandings that later become complaints, disenrollments and reversed enrollments
pros.example: asking a member to describe in her own words what will happen to her pharmacy in January surfaces that she believed her current pharmacy stays preferred, before anything is signed

cons.claim: The discipline is slow and sometimes ends with no decision at all, which is costly in a compressed annual window
cons.example: postponing a review so an authorized daughter can join a three-way call can push the member past the days the agent had budgeted for that whole segment

failure_modes: taking a family member's word for the beneficiary's wishes because it is faster
reading confusion as agreement when the member goes quiet and says yes to everything
using a real plan change as a fear lever because it happens to be true
continuing to call a member who has asked not to be called
acceptance_tests: the file shows a comprehension check in the member's own words on every decision-bearing contact
no third party is recorded as directing a decision without a member authorization dated before that contact
contact-preference and do-not-contact entries are honored in the outreach lists actually used
revisit_triggers: a member shows new signs of impairment or a caregiver begins speaking for them
an authorized representative, power of attorney or guardianship is asserted or withdrawn
state or federal guidance on protected-consumer contact is updated

nodes.definition: Detect the exact moment an ordinary service conversation turns into a marketing or sales contact, and stop there. The observable triggers are concrete: the member asks what else is out there, the agent names a specific alternative plan, a benefit of another product is described, the conversation moves from using current coverage to changing it, or a third party joins asking about switching. At that point the required permission and appointment artifacts must already exist for the product categories about to be discussed; if they do not, the conversation pauses and the artifact is obtained first, with the record showing who raised the topic. What this unit owns is the detection and the stop; the naming, form and retention of the artifacts belong to the marketing-rules KB, and the window determination that follows belongs to the enrollment KB.

included: the observable triggers that cross from servicing into marketing
the stop-and-obtain-artifact reflex mid-call
recording who introduced the plan-change topic
excluded: the content and retention rules of the artifacts themselves
period eligibility determination
the plan comparison that follows

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the appointment or permission requirements, or an audit finding about how a conversation was initiated

pros.claim: Catching the crossing in the moment keeps an otherwise good enrollment from being unusable and keeps a helpful call from becoming an unpermitted sales contact
pros.example: a member calls about a lost card and mentions her neighbor's plan; the agent finishes the card issue, explains that discussing another plan needs the proper appointment on record, and schedules it

cons.claim: Stopping a conversation the member started feels obstructive to someone who just wants an answer now
cons.example: a member who asks 'so should I switch?' hears 'I have to get a form from you first' and reads it as bureaucracy rather than protection

failure_modes: letting momentum carry a service call into a plan comparison because the member seemed to invite it
treating a member-initiated question as a blanket waiver of the artifact requirement
obtaining the artifact after the discussion and backdating the sequence in the record
acceptance_tests: for every plan-change discussion in the book, the required artifact is dated before the discussion it covers
the contact log records which party raised the alternative-plan topic
servicing calls that touched a plan question show either an artifact or a documented pause and reschedule
revisit_triggers: the marketing or appointment artifact rules change for the plan year
a carrier or regulator questions how a plan-change conversation began
servicing volume rises enough that calls are being handled without file access

nodes.definition: Maintain one current, retrievable file per member that the whole practice runs on: plan and effective date by carrier; the providers, drugs and pharmacy that justified the fit at enrollment and their current state; the permission and appointment artifacts with their dates; every contact with date, channel, topic and outcome; open service items with an owner and a promised date; authorized-contact and representative designations; and the status flags — subsidy or Medicaid status, institutional status, address and county — that change what is possible next. The file is the substrate for reconciliation, triage, annual review and persistency reading alike, and it is kept to the minimum necessary information handled under the privacy obligations that apply. It is not the audit-file standard, which is defined in the marketing and documentation KB; this is the operating record the servicing day is run from.

included: per-member plan, provider, drug and pharmacy state
contact log and open service items with owners and dates
authorization and status flags that gate later action
excluded: the retention schedule and audit-file standard
carrier systems of record
storing clinical detail beyond what servicing requires

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a servicing failure traced to stale or missing file data, or a privacy obligation change affecting what may be stored

pros.claim: A file that already holds the drug and provider list turns an annual review from an interview into a check, which is the only way a one-person book gets reviewed in the window at all
pros.example: the agent opens a member's file in early autumn, compares the plan's change notice against the five drugs and two specialists already recorded, and calls with a specific answer rather than a questionnaire

cons.claim: The record decays silently and gives false confidence, because drugs and providers change without anyone telling the agent
cons.example: a file still lists a discontinued medication, so the autumn comparison clears a plan whose formulary change actually hits the member's new prescription

failure_modes: keeping the real state of a member in the agent's head or a phone's call history
capturing more sensitive detail than servicing needs and creating a privacy exposure
logging contacts without outcomes, so an open item is never closed by anyone
acceptance_tests: any member in the book can be opened to a current plan, provider, drug and pharmacy state plus the date each was last confirmed
every open service item carries an owner and a promised date, and closed items carry an outcome
authorization records exist for every third party who has directed anything
revisit_triggers: a member reports a new prescription, prescriber, pharmacy or address
a carrier notice or returned mail contradicts the recorded state
the annual review finds file data older than one plan year

nodes.definition: Hold the shape of how money arrives on an enrolled member, without holding any remembered figure. The mechanism has identifiable parts: a product class that determines which compensation regime applies at all; a regulated maximum for that class and market that is republished on a cycle; the carrier's own contracted rate within that ceiling; the member's history, which decides whether the initial or the renewal level applies; a payment path that may run through an upline or field organization before reaching the agent; and a payment cycle keyed to effective dates and carrier reporting. Some products in an agent's mix are compensated on entirely different administrative or fee arrangements, so each product is classified before anything is assumed. The expert's discipline is to verify the current-year values in the applicable published schedule and in each carrier's own compensation addendum, per plan year, and to treat any number heard from a recruiter or remembered from last year as unverified.

included: the parts of the mechanism and what moves each
product-class classification before assuming a regime
where current-year values are verified
excluded: stating any specific amount, rate or multiple
negotiating contract terms
tax treatment of the income

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: publication of the plan-year schedule or a carrier compensation addendum that changes a class, ceiling, level definition or payment path

pros.claim: Knowing the mechanism rather than a number makes the agent immune to recruiting illustrations and to the annual surprise of a changed schedule
pros.example: when an upline pitches a book move on the strength of a payout claim, the agent asks which product class, which schedule year and which addendum clause that figure comes from, and reads it before deciding

cons.claim: The mechanism has genuinely moving parts across carriers and years, so mastering it costs real reading time every plan year and is never finished
cons.example: three carriers publishing three differently structured addenda in the same autumn as certification season competes for the same hours

failure_modes: carrying last year's understanding into the new plan year
assuming every product in the mix pays under the same regime
planning a practice around an upline's illustration rather than a signed addendum
acceptance_tests: for each product class the agent sells, the current-year schedule reference and the carrier addendum clause governing payment are on file and dated
no compensation statement used in planning traces to memory or to a verbal claim
the payment path, including any pass-through, is written down per carrier
revisit_triggers: the applicable schedule for the coming plan year is published
a carrier issues a new or amended compensation addendum
the agent adds a product class or changes upline

nodes.definition: Determine, for each member individually, which payment level applies and whether payment continues at all — the question that decides most of a book's income and almost none of its advice. The determination reads the member's own history: whether they are new to the product class, continuously enrolled without a break, moving between plans in a way the rules treat as preserving the level, or returning after a gap; and it reads the events that stop payment entirely, such as disenrollment, termination for non-payment, loss of eligibility or death. Because these classes are defined by rule and restated each plan year, the determination is made per member per year against current guidance, written into the member file, and then reconciled against what the carrier actually pays — a mismatch is a signal about one of the three, not proof about any of them.

included: per-member level determination from enrollment history
the event classes that end continuation
recording the determination for later reconciliation
excluded: using the determination in any recommendation
stating what a level pays
the carrier's internal crediting logic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: restated plan-year guidance on level and continuation classes, or a cohort-wide mismatch between determinations and paid statements

pros.claim: A per-member determination turns statement variance from a mystery into a checkable expectation
pros.example: a member whose history shows a break in coverage is expected at the initial level, so when the statement shows the other level the agent knows which of the two records to question

cons.claim: The classes are technical and change, so an agent can be confidently wrong across a whole cohort at once
cons.example: misreading how one class of plan-to-plan move is treated produces the same wrong expectation on every member who made that move that autumn

failure_modes: applying a rule of thumb from a prior year to the current one
inferring level from what was paid rather than determining it from history and checking the payment
letting the determination influence what the member is told about staying or moving
acceptance_tests: each member file carries a level determination for the current plan year with the history facts it rests on
the determination is dated and cites the guidance class used, not a remembered rule
no determination note appears in any member-facing recommendation
revisit_triggers: current-year guidance restates how a move class is treated
a member's enrollment history changes through a move, a break or a retroactive correction
statement reconciliation shows a level mismatch on more than an isolated member

nodes.definition: Treat agent-of-record as a carrier-side attribute rather than a description of the relationship. It is set by the accepted enrollment and can move when the member enrolls through another agent, through a carrier's own line, or through a public enrollment channel; it can be absent when a writing agent leaves, is terminated or lets an appointment lapse, leaving the member an orphan. Servicing someone loyally does not create or restore the attribute. The work is operational: verify status per member in each carrier's agent portal on a fixed cycle; notice silent losses, where a member simply stops appearing on a statement with no notice; know what each carrier's process and evidence requirements are for a change request and what the current rules permit an agent to ask a member to do; and decide deliberately how to serve members the agent will not be paid on, since abandoning them is both a reputational and an ethical failure.

included: periodic status verification per carrier
detection of silent losses and orphan status
deliberate service policy for unpaid members
excluded: pressuring or coaching a member to name the agent
the carrier's internal crediting rules
disputes over another agent's conduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier change to attribution or change-request handling, or a cluster of unexplained attribution losses in one cohort

pros.claim: Regular verification converts an invisible income leak into a dated event with a cause, which is the only way a dispute is ever winnable
pros.example: a quarterly portal check shows three members no longer attributed, and the enrollment dates point at a specific event rather than a general suspicion

cons.claim: Status checking across several carrier portals is tedious manual work that competes with servicing time and produces nothing a member ever sees
cons.example: an hour per carrier per quarter spent reconciling attribution lists is an hour not spent on the review queue

failure_modes: assuming a long relationship guarantees attribution
discovering a loss only when the income is already gone for a full cycle
reacting to a loss by pressuring the member instead of asking what need went unmet
acceptance_tests: attribution status is verified per carrier on a stated cycle and the check date is recorded
each detected loss has a recorded date, suspected cause class and the service response taken
the practice has a written policy for serving orphan or unattributed members
revisit_triggers: a member disappears from a carrier statement without a disenrollment notice
a carrier changes its attribution or change-request process
the agent's appointment status changes with any carrier

nodes.definition: Understand how money already received can be taken back, and where that exposure is actually created. The mechanism classes are recognizable: a member disenrolls or is terminated early within the period the rules define for recovery; a termination is applied retroactively for non-payment or lost eligibility; an enrollment is reversed after a beneficiary complaint or a directed correction; or a payment level is reclassified after the fact. The exposure is mostly manufactured upstream, at the moment of a rushed or over-promised enrollment, and it surfaces months later with a lag that makes the connection easy to miss. The operating stance is: know each carrier's recovery terms as contract classes and verify them as signed; expect the lag and never treat a paid statement as final; never let recoupment risk shape what a member is told; and read a rising pattern of reversals as a defect in fit or process rather than as bad luck.

included: the mechanism classes that reverse payment
the lag between event and reversal
reading reversal patterns as an upstream defect signal
excluded: letting exposure influence advice to a member
carrier accounting internals
any figure for a recovery amount or period

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: amended carrier recovery terms, or a measured rise in reversals within an identifiable cohort

pros.claim: Treating reversals as a diagnostic rather than an accident points straight at the enrollment conversations that were oversold
pros.example: reversals concentrated in members enrolled in the final days of the window indicate rushed fit checks rather than a carrier problem

cons.claim: Awareness of exposure creates a standing temptation to discourage a member from a move that is right for them
cons.example: an agent hesitating to explain a genuinely better fit in the first months after enrollment because the reversal would land on their own statement

failure_modes: treating a paid statement as settled money and spending against it
arguing a member out of an early change to protect a payment
recording reversals as noise instead of tracing each to a cause class
acceptance_tests: each carrier's recovery terms are recorded from the signed agreement with the date read
every reversal in the book is traced to a cause class and cohorted by enrollment month and source
no file shows a member being discouraged from a change during a recovery-exposed period
revisit_triggers: a carrier amends its recovery terms
reversal frequency rises in any cohort, plan or enrollment source
current-year guidance changes the recovery period classes

nodes.definition: Run a fixed-cycle comparison between what each carrier and pass-through entity reports paying and what the agent's own member ledger says should be there. The comparison is at member level, never at total level: is the expected line present; is it at the level the per-member determination predicted; do the effective date and member identifiers match; is every reversal explained by a known event; and does every missing line resolve to a cause class such as an attribution loss, a late carrier report, a pass-through delay, a disenrollment, or an application that never processed. Disputes are evidence-driven — application confirmation, submission receipt, effective date, attribution evidence — and are filed inside the window the carrier's own process states. An aggregate total that looks approximately right is not evidence of anything.

included: member-level statement comparison on a fixed cycle
cause classification for missing or wrong lines
evidence-based dispute inside the carrier's stated window
excluded: accounting, bookkeeping and tax treatment
renegotiating contracted rates
disputes about another agent's attribution conduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier statement format or cadence change, or a reconciliation cycle in which unmatched lines rise materially

pros.claim: Member-level reconciliation is the only way an unattributed or unprocessed member is found while a dispute is still possible
pros.example: an application that was accepted but never appeared on a statement is caught in the next cycle, when the confirmation number and submission receipt are still retrievable

cons.claim: The work is unglamorous, monthly, and expands with every carrier added, and it produces nothing a member values
cons.example: a book across five carriers means five different statement formats and identifier conventions to normalize by hand every cycle

failure_modes: checking totals rather than lines and never noticing a systematically missing cohort
discovering a discrepancy after the carrier's dispute window has closed
assuming any missing line is a carrier error rather than testing the attribution and processing causes
acceptance_tests: every statement cycle is reconciled at member level with unmatched lines listed and assigned a cause class
each dispute filed cites the specific evidence and the date it was submitted
the ledger of expected members is derived from the member files, not from the prior statement
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes statement format, identifiers or reporting cadence
the unmatched-line count rises above its usual level
a pass-through entity changes how or when it remits

nodes.definition: Model the shape of the practice's income rather than its size. The shape is produced by identifiable mechanisms: new-enrollment payments cluster after the effective dates that follow the annual window; renewal payments arrive on an anniversary cadence that differs by carrier and product; every payment lags submission by the carrier's processing and reporting time; a pass-through entity adds another step; and reversals land after the fact, subtracting from a later cycle than the one they belong to. The planning output is deliberately qualitative — which parts of the year are heavier and leaner in relative terms, and how much runway the leaner stretch requires — built from the agent's own verified statements over time rather than from projections. Its real purpose is ethical as much as financial: an agent who is under cash pressure during the annual window is an agent under pressure to move members.

included: the timing mechanisms that shape income across a year
relative heavier and leaner bands built from verified statements
runway planning as a pressure-reduction control
excluded: stating projected income figures or multiples
tax, accounting and financing advice
using expected income to prioritize which members are served

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: two consecutive cycles diverging from the modeled timing, or a carrier or product mix change that alters the payment calendar

pros.claim: Naming the lean stretch in advance removes the financial pressure that makes steering tempting in the busiest weeks of the year
pros.example: an agent who has planned for the gap between the annual window and the first payments on new effective dates enters that window able to tell members their plan still fits

cons.claim: Timing patterns are only as good as the history behind them and shift whenever the carrier mix or a reporting cadence changes
cons.example: adding a carrier whose renewal anniversary cycle differs from the rest reshapes the year's pattern before the agent has a year of data on it

failure_modes: planning against a projection instead of the practice's own verified history
treating reversals as though they land in the period they arose
letting a lean stretch dictate which members get contacted
acceptance_tests: the income-shape model is built only from reconciled statements and states its bands qualitatively
the plan names the lean stretch and the runway held against it
no servicing or review priority in the practice is traceable to the income calendar
revisit_triggers: the carrier mix changes or a new product class is added
a carrier changes payment cadence or reporting lag
an actual cycle diverges from the modeled shape for two consecutive periods

nodes.definition: Classify every inbound issue before working it, along four axes: who can actually resolve it (carrier member services, the pharmacy, the provider's billing office, the Social Security Administration, the federal Medicare help line, the state counseling program, or the agent); how clock-sensitive it is (a printed appeal deadline, an effective-date cutoff, a medication the member is out of today); whether it touches an election, in which case it stops until permission and appointment artifacts are in place and the window question goes to the enrollment path; and how severe it is for this member given their segment. The output is a routed item with a named owner, a next action, a promised callback time and a file entry. Triage exists because attention is the real constraint in a book of any size, and because misrouting produces both member harm and rework in the same motion.

included: resolver, clock, election-touch and severity classification
routing with named owner and promised callback
the stop rule when an issue becomes an election question
excluded: performing the resolution the carrier or provider owns
period determination
clinical or coverage determinations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: missed callbacks, a recurring unroutable issue class, or a change in which channel owns a resolution

pros.claim: Classifying the resolver first prevents hours spent chasing something only the carrier or a federal agency can do
pros.example: a premium-withholding problem routed to the Social Security Administration on the first call instead of after three calls to carrier member services

cons.claim: Triage adds a step that feels like delay to a member who wants the agent to just fix it now
cons.example: a member describing a pharmacy rejection hears questions about which pharmacy and which notice before hearing an answer

failure_modes: starting work on the first issue described rather than the most clock-critical one
promising a callback with no owner or date and losing the item
handling an election-adjacent question conversationally because it arrived inside a service call
acceptance_tests: every intake records resolver, clock sensitivity, election-touch flag, owner and promised callback
clock-critical items are worked ahead of scheduled outreach on the same day
election-touch items show either the required artifact or a documented pause
revisit_triggers: callback promises begin to be missed
a new issue class appears repeatedly and has no routing rule
the marketing or appointment artifact rules change

nodes.definition: Handle the most common mid-year shock in this book: a doctor, hospital or group is suddenly out of network, or the member has been told they are. Confirm the fact at the source before advising anything, because the member's account and the provider's front desk are often both wrong — check the carrier's current directory and get member services to state it, and check with the provider's billing office rather than the receptionist. Then establish the member's actual exposure under the plan they hold: which services are affected, what in-network alternatives exist, whether any continuity-of-care or transition provision the carrier offers might apply, and what the out-of-network cost consequence is under that plan type. Explain all of it educationally. If a remedy would require an enrollment action, the eligibility and window determination goes to the enrollment path with permissions re-established — never assert that a network change automatically creates a right to change plans.

included: source confirmation of the network fact
exposure analysis under the member's current plan type
educational explanation and clean handoff of any election question
excluded: asserting an enrollment right or determining a window
negotiating with providers or carriers on the member's behalf
advising the member which doctor to see

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier-provider contract event affecting the service area, or a change in the carrier's stated continuity-of-care handling

pros.claim: Confirming at the source prevents a whole cascade of advice built on a rumor at a front desk
pros.example: a member told at check-in that the plan is no longer accepted turns out to have a billing-system issue rather than a contract termination, and no plan change was ever needed

cons.claim: Verification takes days the member experiences as inaction while they are frightened about losing their doctor
cons.example: waiting for a written confirmation from member services while the member is calling daily about a scheduled procedure

failure_modes: advising from a directory entry alone when directories lag real contract status
implying an election right exists because the disruption feels unfair
leaving the member to work out the cost consequence of the plan type on their own
acceptance_tests: every network claim acted on is confirmed at the carrier and the provider, with the confirmation dated in the file
the member's exposure is explained in terms of their own plan type before any option is discussed
any election question is handed off with the artifact and the handoff recorded
revisit_triggers: a carrier and provider contract dispute becomes public in the service area
several members report the same provider or group as affected
the carrier publishes a continuity-of-care or transition provision change

nodes.definition: Work the call that begins 'my medication cost went up' by diagnosing which mechanism produced it before offering anything. The candidate causes are distinguishable: a formulary or tier change at the plan-year boundary, movement between coverage phases as the year's spending accumulates, a newly applied utilization-management requirement such as prior authorization or step therapy, a pharmacy that is no longer preferred or no longer in network, a change or loss in a low-income subsidy or Medicaid status, or simply a new prescription. Each cause has legitimate routes: a pharmacy comparison, a conversation between the member and the prescriber about a covered alternative, the plan's exception or appeal process, manufacturer or state assistance programs, or a subsidy screening through official channels. The agent explains mechanisms and connects the member to the right channel; the agent never selects a medication, never promises a coverage outcome, and never completes clinical paperwork.

included: differential diagnosis of the cost-change mechanism
routing to pharmacy, prescriber, plan process or assistance channels
screening prompts toward official subsidy channels
excluded: choosing or recommending a drug or therapeutic substitution
predicting an exception or appeal outcome
completing or signing clinical documentation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: plan-year formulary and cost-sharing changes, or a cluster of identical cost events on one plan indicating a structural change rather than individual causes

pros.claim: Naming the mechanism turns panic into a specific, workable next step and often ends with no plan change at all
pros.example: a member's increase traced to a preferred-pharmacy change is resolved by transferring the prescription rather than by anything to do with coverage

cons.claim: Diagnosis needs current formulary and status facts the agent cannot see directly, so it depends on the member relaying documents accurately under stress
cons.example: a member who cannot find the pharmacy receipt or the plan notice leaves the agent guessing between a tier change and a phase transition

failure_modes: jumping to a plan change as the first answer to a pharmacy-counter problem
stating that a drug will be covered or an exception will succeed
missing a subsidy or Medicaid status change that explains the whole event
acceptance_tests: each drug-cost event in the file records the cause class identified and the evidence used
the route offered matches the cause class and no file shows a drug being selected by the agent
subsidy-related causes are routed to official screening channels and the referral is recorded
revisit_triggers: the plan year turns and formularies and cost-sharing reset
a member's subsidy or Medicaid status changes
a cluster of members on one plan reports the same cost change

nodes.definition: Support a member facing a denied claim or an unexpected bill without stepping outside the agent's role. Start from the actual document — the denial notice or the explanation of benefits — rather than the member's summary of it, because the stated reason determines everything that follows. Classify that reason: a non-covered service, an out-of-network encounter, a missing authorization, a coding or billing error, or an eligibility mismatch. Protect the deadline printed on the notice as the first-order fact. Then route: the provider's billing office for coding and eligibility errors, the carrier for coverage determinations, the plan's formal appeal and grievance process for denials the member wants to contest, and the state counseling program or the carrier's advocacy channel when the member needs help the agent cannot give. The agent may explain the process, help assemble documents where the member authorizes it, and follow up; the agent does not act as appointed representative, argue medical necessity, or predict outcomes.

included: obtaining and reading the actual notice
reason classification and deadline protection
routing to billing office, carrier, formal appeal process or counseling program
excluded: serving as appointed representative
arguing clinical necessity or interpreting medical policy
predicting the outcome of an appeal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the appeal or grievance process classes, or a pattern of denials of one service class within a plan

pros.claim: Deadline protection alone preserves rights that quietly expire while everyone is on the phone about something else
pros.example: reading the appeal-by date off the notice on the first call and scheduling the follow-up against it, before any discussion of whether the denial was fair

cons.claim: The boundary disappoints a member who wanted an advocate and does not distinguish an agent from a representative
cons.example: explaining that the appeal form must come from the member or an appointed representative to someone who trusts the agent to handle everything

failure_modes: advising from the member's paraphrase and misreading the actual denial reason
discovering the deadline after it has passed
drifting into arguing medical necessity because the member's situation is sympathetic
acceptance_tests: the actual notice is in the file before any advice about it is recorded
the printed deadline is recorded with the follow-up scheduled against it
no file shows the agent acting as representative or asserting a coverage outcome
revisit_triggers: appeal or grievance process rules change for the plan year
a member asks the agent to sign or file on their behalf
several members report denials of the same service class on one plan

nodes.definition: Notice, on purpose, the life events that change what coverage is possible or what it costs: a move across county or state lines, gaining or losing employer or union coverage, gaining or losing Medicaid or a low-income subsidy, entering or leaving a facility, a death in the household, a lapse or change in how a premium is paid, or a new diagnosis that changes which providers matter. The detection sources are ordinary — the annual review, any servicing call, returned mail, a carrier notice, a member's own update — but only if someone is listening for them. The work is: detect, record in the member file, tell the member plainly what class of question this raises for their coverage, and route the eligibility and window determination to the enrollment path. No window is determined and no plan is recommended in this node; the value here is that the event is caught at all, before it becomes a coverage gap.

included: the detectable status-change classes and their detection sources
recording the change and its date
routing the eligibility question to the enrollment path
excluded: determining any enrollment window or eligibility
recommending a plan in response to the change
verifying the member's status with government agencies on their behalf

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a coverage gap or late transition traced to a status change that was audible in an earlier call but never recorded

pros.claim: Catching a status change early is often the difference between an orderly transition and a gap in coverage the member pays for
pros.example: a member mentioning in a routine call that a spouse's retirement is coming lets the coverage question be routed months before anything lapses

cons.claim: Surveillance depends on members volunteering personal changes and on the agent asking without becoming intrusive
cons.example: a member who moved to a daughter's home in another county three months ago and never thought to mention it because nothing seemed to break

failure_modes: hearing a status change in a call and not recording it because the call was about something else
answering the window question directly instead of routing it
letting returned mail and carrier notices pile up unread
acceptance_tests: every recorded status change carries a date, a source and the routing action taken
returned mail and carrier notices are worked into the file on a stated cycle
no window determination or plan recommendation appears in a status-change record
revisit_triggers: a member reports a move, a coverage change or a subsidy status change
mail returns or a carrier notice indicates an address or eligibility problem
the annual review surfaces a change that was never recorded

nodes.definition: Handle the cases where the member was actually let down — a promised callback that never came, an application submitted with the wrong effective date, a confident statement about a drug's coverage that proved wrong, a carrier processing failure the agent did not chase. The sequence is acknowledgement first and quickly, in plain words and without deflection onto the carrier; then a clear account of what happened and what is being done; then the fix or escalation with a named owner and a date the member can hold; then a record of the whole thing, including whether the failure must be reported to the carrier or handled through a formal complaint channel, whose process belongs to the compliance KB. Recovery is treated as first-class work because an older beneficiary who felt abandoned during a coverage problem is the disenrollment, the complaint and the reputational loss that no amount of marketing offsets.

included: prompt acknowledgement and plain explanation
owned and dated repair or escalation
recording the failure and deciding whether it must be reported
excluded: the formal complaint and allegation process with carriers and regulators
compensating a member for a loss, which is not the agent's to offer
legal admissions or settlements

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a repeated failure class, or a complaint that reveals members experienced a failure the practice never recorded

pros.claim: Fast honest acknowledgement usually keeps the relationship and almost always keeps the problem from becoming a formal complaint
pros.example: calling a member the same day to say an effective date was submitted wrong, what the correction path is and who is chasing it, rather than waiting for the card not to arrive

cons.claim: Acknowledging error creates real exposure and takes discipline when the failure was partly the carrier's
cons.example: explaining an error plainly to a member whose family is already unhappy, knowing the account may be repeated to a carrier

failure_modes: going quiet on the member while trying to fix it privately
blaming the carrier for something the practice controlled
fixing the instance and never changing the process that produced it
acceptance_tests: every recorded failure has an acknowledgement date, an owner, a repair or escalation path and an outcome
the file states whether reporting was required and what was done
recurring failure classes appear in the practice's process changes, not only in individual files
revisit_triggers: the same failure class occurs twice in a quarter
a member or family member signals intent to complain
a carrier reports a service failure the agent did not know about

nodes.definition: Run the yearly cycle in which each member's current plan is re-checked against their own doctors, drugs, pharmacy and costs as the plan's annual change notice and the next year's plan information become available. The order matters: prepare from the member file before making contact; contact only within the permitted communication rules and through channels the member consented to; walk the member through what is changing on the plan they already hold before any alternative is mentioned; and discuss a specific alternative only with the required appointment artifact already in place. 'Your plan still fits and there is nothing to do' is a complete, successful and documented outcome. The cycle is also a capacity problem: a book cannot be reviewed in the final week of the window, so the queue is built and sequenced weeks earlier, with the highest-need segments first.

included: preparation from the file and review sequencing
walking the member's own plan changes first
documenting a no-change outcome as a real result
queue capacity planning ahead of the window
excluded: the enrollment comparison method and window determination
the communication-rule catalog itself
any review ordering driven by expected payment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: publication of plan-year change notices and plan data, or a review cycle that failed to reach part of the book

pros.claim: A file-prepared review makes the conversation specific to that member's own drugs and doctors, which is what makes members stay and what makes a no-change answer credible
pros.example: opening with 'your plan's notice changes the tier on one of your five drugs and both specialists stay in network' rather than asking the member to describe their situation again

cons.claim: The cycle concentrates most of the year's work into a few weeks that collide with the service desk and with certification obligations
cons.example: the review queue, inbound service calls about the same change notices, and carrier deadlines all landing in the same fortnight

failure_modes: reviewing only the members whose change would produce a payment
leading with an alternative plan before explaining the member's own plan changes
starting the queue so late that the last members are reviewed in a rush or not at all
treating a no-change outcome as a wasted call and not documenting it
acceptance_tests: every member in the book has a dated review outcome for the plan year, including explicit no-change outcomes
each review record shows preparation from the file and the member's own plan changes covered first
any specific alternative discussed has its appointment artifact dated before the discussion
the review queue's order can be explained by member need and timing rather than by expected payment
revisit_triggers: annual change notices or next-year plan data are published
a carrier discontinues or exits a plan held by part of the book
communication or appointment rules change for the plan year
the queue's completion rate falls behind the schedule set before the window

nodes.definition: Sort the book by service need rather than by expected payment, and give each segment a contact rhythm that fits inside consent and communication rules. The segments that matter in this business are recognizable: members in their first months on a new plan, when confusion and reversal risk are highest; members with complex or high-cost drug regimens; members whose providers are in network-fragile arrangements; members whose subsidy, Medicaid or institutional status is subject to redetermination; members who need language, hearing or cognitive support; and stable low-need members who mostly want to know the agent still exists. Each segment gets a defined touch pattern, a topic for each touch, and an intake path. Cadence is simultaneously a capacity statement: it is what tells an agent how large a book one person can serve honestly before quality quietly decays.

included: need-based segmentation of the book
per-segment contact rhythm and topics within consent
capacity sizing implied by the cadence
excluded: segmenting or prioritizing by expected compensation
contact outside the member's consented channels
marketing campaigns and their rule set

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: missed cadence commitments, book growth beyond current capacity, or persistency evidence that a segment is under-served

pros.claim: A need-based cadence puts the agent in front of a problem before the member is angry about it, which is the cheapest retention there is
pros.example: a check-in with newly enrolled members in their first weeks catches card, pharmacy and premium-setup problems while they are still trivial to fix

cons.claim: Any cadence is an outreach program, and outreach to a protected population is exactly where contact rules and member annoyance both live
cons.example: a quarterly courtesy call pattern that a member experiences as being sold to, or that reaches someone who asked not to be called

failure_modes: segmenting by what a member is worth rather than by what a member needs
designing a cadence larger than the practice can actually deliver
ignoring recorded contact preferences when building outreach lists
acceptance_tests: every member is assigned to a segment with a defined touch pattern and topic
the total cadence is reconciled against available servicing hours and the annual window load
outreach lists are filtered by consent and contact-preference records before use
revisit_triggers: the book grows or the carrier mix changes
cadence commitments are missed for a segment two periods running
communication or consent rules change
persistency findings show a segment leaving disproportionately

nodes.definition: Treat retention as a consequence of two things — the plan still fitting and someone reliably answering the phone — and never as a tactic applied to a member. The legitimate levers are named and worked: accurate expectation-setting at enrollment so the first surprise is not a shock, responsiveness on the service desk, proactive contact before pain arrives, an honest annual review that permits a no-change outcome, and clean escalation when something breaks. Equally named is what must never be used: implying that a member cannot change plans or agents, urgency or fear framing, discouraging a member from calling the carrier or the federal help line, withholding information about an option that fits better, or obstructing a move that serves the member. The asymmetry is deliberate: pressure tactics in this vertical are both prohibited and self-defeating, because the members most susceptible to them are precisely the ones whose complaint carries the most weight.

included: the legitimate retention levers and how they are worked
the prohibited-practice list specific to keeping a member
the stance that a member leaving for a better fit is an acceptable outcome
excluded: retention campaigns built on urgency or exclusivity
contractual lock-in of any kind
the marketing-rule catalog itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint alleging pressure, or persistency movement that cannot be explained by structural causes

pros.claim: Service-based retention compounds, because the same behavior that keeps a member also produces the referrals and the clean audit trail
pros.example: a member who was called back the same day about a pharmacy rejection stays, tells a neighbor, and describes the episode accurately if a carrier ever asks

cons.claim: It is slower and less controllable than pressure, and it accepts losing members whose needs are now better served elsewhere
cons.example: helping a member understand an option only available through another route, knowing the attribution and the renewal go with them

failure_modes: letting a defensive instinct produce urgency language during a difficult call
discouraging a member from contacting the carrier or the federal help line
measuring retention as a target and quietly reintroducing pressure to hit it
acceptance_tests: no member-facing communication in the book uses urgency, exclusivity or fear framing to keep a member
cases where a member's better option lay elsewhere show the option being explained rather than obscured
retention is reported alongside its causes rather than as a bare number to be maximized
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleges pressure or obstruction
persistency drops in a segment without a structural explanation
a competitor's tactics in the service area create pressure to respond in kind

nodes.definition: Read who left, when and why as an instrument rather than as a scoreboard. Separate the exits into classes that mean different things: structural exits the practice never controlled, such as death, a move, a plan leaving the market or a Medicaid status change; fit failures, where a drug was not covered, a doctor was out of network or a cost was not what the member expected; service failures, where calls went unanswered or an issue was never resolved; and attribution losses, where the member stayed but the agent-of-record position moved. Cohort the leavers by enrollment source, plan, enrollment month and segment, and look for the pattern rather than reacting to the loudest anecdote. Each class routes work upstream: fit failures back into the needs and comparison practice, service failures into cadence and triage, source-linked failures into the lead-source and marketing decisions that another KB owns.

included: exit classification into structural, fit, service and attribution classes
cohorting by source, plan, month and segment
routing each finding to the upstream practice that owns it
excluded: acting on lead-source and marketing decisions, which belong to the marketing KB
changing the comparison method itself, which belongs to the enrollment KB
publishing member-identifiable analysis

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a completed post-window exit analysis, or a cohort whose exit rate departs from the practice's established range

pros.claim: Classified exits convert a vague sense that the year went badly into one or two specific, fixable upstream defects
pros.example: finding that most fit-failure exits came from one enrollment source and one month points at how those enrollments were conducted rather than at the plan itself

cons.claim: Exit reasons are partly unknowable, since members who leave quietly rarely explain themselves accurately or at all
cons.example: an exit recorded as structural because the member mentioned moving, when the real reason was three unreturned calls the previous spring

failure_modes: counting exits without classifying them and concluding nothing
reacting to a single vivid complaint as though it were the pattern
diagnosing correctly and never routing the finding to the practice that must change
acceptance_tests: every exit in the period carries a class and the evidence behind the classification
the analysis is cohorted by at least source, plan and enrollment month
each identified defect has a named upstream practice and a change recorded against it
revisit_triggers: the annual window closes and the year's exits can be counted
a cohort's exits rise above the practice's normal range
reversal or attribution-loss counts move independently of enrollment volume

nodes.definition: Grow from a well-served book without breaking the two rule families that govern it: how a beneficiary may be contacted, and what may be given or received for a referral. In practice this means the member may tell whoever they like about the agent, but the agent may not contact a referred person until that person has given their own permission to be contacted; may not offer or accept anything of value that would constitute a prohibited inducement, with any nominal-item allowance treated as a rule to verify for the current year rather than a remembered figure; may not use one member's protected information to reach another; and does not turn a service call with a vulnerable member into a referral solicitation. The economic argument for doing it this way is not merely legal: referred members arrive with accurate expectations set by someone they trust, which shows up later as better fit and fewer early reversals.

included: permission-first contact of a referred person
the inducement boundary and the duty to verify current allowances
keeping referral requests out of vulnerable-member service calls
excluded: paid lead generation and vendor arrangements
marketing events and their rule set
any specific value or figure for a permitted nominal item

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: restated inducement or contact rules for the plan year, or a complaint traced to a referral-sourced contact

pros.claim: Permission-first referral is the lowest-risk growth channel available in this vertical and produces the best-fitting members
pros.example: a member gives the agent's number to a neighbour who then calls in and gives permission directly, so contact starts from the beneficiary's own initiative

cons.claim: It is slow, unschedulable, and depends entirely on service quality the agent cannot surge on demand
cons.example: a lean year cannot be fixed by asking the book for referrals, because the referrals that arrive were earned in previous years

failure_modes: calling a referred person on the referrer's say-so alone
offering a gift or thank-you that crosses the inducement line
asking for referrals during a call about the member's own coverage crisis
using member information to identify and approach a household member
acceptance_tests: every referred contact is preceded by that person's own recorded permission
any item of value given or received is checked against the current-year rule and the check is documented
no referral request appears in a service call about an unresolved member problem
revisit_triggers: inducement or contact rules are restated for the plan year
a referral source produces a cluster of poor-fit enrollments
a complaint alleges an unwanted contact traced to a referral

nodes.definition: Be precise about what the agent actually holds. It is not ownership of members: it is a set of carrier appointments and agent-of-record positions, each governed by the terms of a signed carrier or upline agreement — release and assignment provisions, any vesting-class treatment of renewals, what happens to payments after termination or voluntary departure, and whether the position may be transferred to another licensed agent at all. The work is unglamorous and protective: read and keep the actual terms per carrier and upline rather than the version repeated at recruiting meetings; maintain a member record that could be handed to a successor within privacy limits; never promise members permanence the contracts do not support; and hold a continuity plan so that if the agent dies, retires or loses an appointment, the members are served rather than stranded. Any actual sale, transfer or succession arrangement is a matter for qualified legal and tax counsel.

included: reading and keeping the governing contract terms per carrier and upline
a successor-ready member record within privacy limits
a continuity plan for departure, incapacity or lost appointment
excluded: valuing a book or stating any multiple
structuring or executing a sale, which requires legal and tax counsel
promising members that their agent relationship is permanent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an amended or renewed carrier or upline agreement, or a contemplated change of upline, carrier mix or practice ownership

pros.claim: Knowing the actual terms before a move or a departure prevents the discovery that renewals stop the day the relationship ends
pros.example: reading a release provision before agreeing to change upline, rather than after the first statement arrives short

cons.claim: Terms vary by carrier and change on renewal of the agreements, so the reading is never finished and rarely favours the agent
cons.example: two carriers in the same book treating post-termination renewals in opposite ways, so no single continuity rule covers the practice

failure_modes: assuming the book is an owned asset because it feels like one
relying on a recruiter's characterization instead of the signed agreement
leaving no continuity plan, so members are orphaned the moment the agent stops
acceptance_tests: the governing release, assignment and post-termination terms are on file per carrier and upline with the date read
a continuity plan names who serves the book if the agent cannot, and how members would be told
no member-facing statement promises permanence that the agreements do not support
revisit_triggers: a carrier or upline agreement is renewed, amended or replaced
the agent considers changing upline or adding a carrier
an appointment is terminated or lapses

edges.why_related: the duty owed after enrollment is what makes the contact discipline an obligation rather than a preference
neutrality is the operating expression of the duty in every stay-or-move decision the book produces
the crossing point matters most with a protected consumer, so the contact discipline sets how the stop is handled
the per-member level determination is only meaningful once the classes and their sources are mapped
attribution is the part of the mechanism that decides whether any payment reaches this agent at all
what can be reversed depends on which payment level and continuation state the member sits in
a statement can only be reconciled against members the agent is actually attributed on
the income shape is built only from reconciled history, never from projections
triage decisions need the member's plan, providers, drugs and open items in front of the agent
a denial arrives with a printed deadline, which is exactly the clock triage exists to catch
the review is prepared from the file before contact, which is what makes it specific and fast
retention rests on the proactive contact the cadence actually delivers
referrals are earned by service quality and cannot be manufactured when they are needed
the review may not move to a specific alternative plan until the required appointment artifact is in place
neutrality governs both the order of the review queue and the recommendation inside each review
any cadence is outreach to a protected population and is bounded by consent and contact preferences
referral requests may not be made of a member mid-crisis or of a member whose comprehension is in question
what a network disruption is worth to the agent may not shape what the member is told about their options
the role limits set in the frame define exactly how far appeal support may go
detecting a qualifying-looking life event does not license a plan conversation without the artifact
knowing precisely how each outcome pays creates the standing temptation the neutrality rule exists to suppress
edges.resolution_rule: neutrality wins without exception: the mechanism may be used for reconciliation, planning and dispute, and never as an input to what a member is told or which members are contacted
